name: oyren-agent
description: The sandbox agents behind VS Code's built-in Chat view — one chat that combines every CLI agent.
_comment.enabledApiProposals: isDefault + modes on the participant, isUserSelectable/isDefault on the provider's models, and
the chatSessions registration APIs all need proposals at 1.109. Matched against the launcher's
this list into product.json's extensionEnabledApiProposals: that key OVERRIDES an extension's
own declaration rather than merging with it.

_comment.chatParticipants: The default participant is the LAUNCH agent and claims all three modes: the panel opens in
Agent mode (hardcoded default), and getDefaultAgent filters by mode — an ask-only default
makes every Agent/Edit-mode send die in a swallowed 'Cannot handle request' with no UI.
Core wraps nothing loop-shaped around an agent-mode participant at 1.109; tool orchestration
is engine-side. isSticky false on purpose: sticky plants '@oyren' into the input on every
turn, and this panel IS the Oyren agent — attribution says so, the input shouldn't.
The named participants back the per-agent chat sessions (sessionProviders.js); they must be
declared here or the main thread silently rejects their registration. claude-code is absent by design: it runs launch-only (SDK engine, no ACP recipe), and a dead dropdown row is worse than none.

chatParticipants.name: oyren
chatParticipants.description: Ask the sandbox agent — one chat for every CLI agent.

_comment.chatSessions: One entry per CLI agent = one row in the chat's agent-type dropdown (on our patched build;
stock builds filter these through a hardcoded allowlist and simply never show them).
type = the runtime's AGENT_KIND ids verbatim — it rides back as ?agent=<type>.
canDelegate:true makes selection open the session IN the chat widget.
